title: Sage Kapila burns the sons of Sagara
introduction: Sage Vishwamitra's narration of Sagara's legend is continued. Sagara's sons dig out all the quarters of earth and when they enter northeast to find out the horse thief, there they find Sage Kapila, i.e., Vishnu in the semblance of a sage. When they wanted to attack that sage Kapila, he renders them to heaps of ashes by his yogic powers.
closing: इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 40th chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
देवतानां वचः श्रुत्वा भगवान्वै पितामहः |
प्रत्युवाच सुसंत्रस्तान् कृतान्तबलमोहितान्
verses.iast:
devatānām vacaḥ śrutvā bhagavān vai pitāmahaḥ |
pratyuvāca susantrastān kṛtānta bala mohitān
verses.translation: "On hearing the words of gods, the esteemed Forefather Brahma spoke to them, who are very highly scared, and bewildered by the might of Sagara's sons for they are effectuating the end of all beings." Vishvamitra thus continued his narration.

glosses.meaning: effectuating, end of [all beings,] by might [of Sagara's sons]
in turn, spoke to - replied = vai = indeed.

verses.devanagari:
यस्येयं वसुधा कृत्स्ना वासुदेवस्य धीमतः|
महिषी माधवस्यैषा स एव भगवान् प्रभुः
कापिलं रूपमास्थाय धारयत्यनिशं धराम् |
तस्य कोपाग्निना दग्धा भविष्यन्ति नृपात्मजाः
verses.iast:
yasya iyam vasudhā kṛtsnā vāsudevasya dhīmataḥ |
mahiṣī mādhavasaya sa eṣā sa eva bhagavan prabhuḥ
kāpilam rūpam āsthāya dhārayatya aniśam dharām |
tasya kopāgninā dagdhā bhaviṣyanti nṛpātmajā
verses.translation: " 'To whom this Mother Earth belongs in all her entirety, he is that prescient Vasudeva, and she is also the consort of that Maadhava, and that Vishnu eternally props up Mother Earth. Hence, that reverential Vishnu donning the semblance of Sage Kapila will burn down the sons of emperor Sagara to ashes in a fire of fury.
notes: The islands / continents on earth, dvīpa-s, are 'jambu- plaksha - shaalmali- kusha - kraunca - shaaka - puSkara. And they are the seven continents. Some say the earth is having nine continents, yet some others prefer eighteen. However entire globe bhū devi belongs to Vishnu as she is his another consort.

glosses.meaning: she is, the consort, of Maadhava
whose [to which,] prescient, belongs to Vaasudeva
sage Kapila's, semblance of, on donning
in his [Kapila's,] fury's, fire, burnt down
they will be - burnt to ashes..

verses.devanagari:
पृथिव्याश्चापि निर्भेदो दृष्ट एव सनातनः |
सगरस्य च पुत्राणां विनाशो दीर्घदर्शिनाम्
verses.iast:
pṛthivyāḥ ca api nirbhedo dṛṣṭa eva sanātanaḥ |
sagarasya ca putrāṇām vināśo dīrgha darśinām
verses.translation: 'Even the complete cleavage of the earth, and the complete ruination of Sagara's sons as well, are envisaged by the providentially farsighted ancients." So said Brahma to gods.
notes: This is the cosmic routine. Every day of Brahma is one kalpa and in each kalpa Brahma starts to create the universe afresh. Though it is just like the bygone creation it is anew, but the presiding souls of each object of the universe will change. If one soul presides the Sun or the Moon in this era, in the next era they attain a higher step in the ladder of 'snakes and ladders' called vaikunṭha pāli and a soul-in-wait takes up the job of that Sun or Moon, just as good as the promotions of officials. In this cosmic destruction even the gods or godlike entities will be destroyed if they tend to cause unnecessary ruination to the living beings anena bahu praṇi upadrava kāriṇām devā api vadha upāyam abhīpsanti - daiva hatānām ca teṣām avicāreṇa nāso bhavatya eveti sūcitam -dk This is the same even in the case of Indra. Vishnu in His Trivikrama incarnation blesses the demonic Emperor Bali with such Indra-hood in some era, when Bali's sin is counted down, and when merit accrues.

verses.devanagari:
पितामह वचः श्रुत्वा त्रयस्त्रिंशदरिन्दम |
देवाः परमसंहृष्टाः पुनर्जग्मुर्यथागतम्
verses.iast:
pitāmaha vacaḥ śrutvā trayaḥ triṃśat arindamaḥ |
devāḥ parama saṃhṛṣṭāḥ punar jagmur yathā āgatam
verses.translation: "On hearing the words of the Forefather Brahma all the thirty three gods went away with utmost satisfaction, as they have came.
notes: The gods that have come to appeal to Brahma are said to be thirty-three in numbers. It is not that all the count of all the gods who have come. There are others besides the prominent groups of thirty-three god-groups. The thirty-three primary god-groups who have come here are aṣṭa vasu-s 'eight Vasu gods' ekādaśa rudrā-s 'eleven Rudra gods' aśvini dvaya twin brothers called 'ashvini-gods,' those that are mostly connected with the administration of earth.

verses.devanagari:
सगरस्य च पुत्राणां प्रादुरासीन्महास्वनः |
पृथिव्यां भिद्यमानायां निर्घातसमनिःस्वनः
verses.iast:
sagarasya ca putrāṇām prādur āsīt mahāsvanaḥ |
pṛthivyām bhidyamānāyām nirghāta sama niḥvanaḥ
verses.translation: "When the sons of Sagara are digging the earth then there emerged an unbearable noise similar to the crashing of a thunder.

verses.devanagari:
ततो भित्त्वा महीं सर्वां कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम् |
सहिताः सगराः सर्वे पितरं वाक्यमब्रुवन्
verses.iast:
tato bhittvā mahīm sarvām kṛtvā ca api pradakṣiṇam |
sahitāḥ sagarāḥ sarve pitaram vākyam abruvan
verses.translation: "Then on hollowing the entire earth, and on making trips around her without finding the horse, all of the sons of Sagara have come together and on going to their father they spoke these words to him.

glosses.meaning: round trips, also, even, on making

verses.devanagari:
परिक्रांता मही सर्वा सत्त्ववन्तश्च सूदिताः |
देवदानवरक्षांसि पिशाचोरगपन्नगाः
न च पश्यामहेऽश्वं तमश्वहर्तारमेव च |
किं करिष्याम भद्रं ते बुद्धिरत्र विचार्यताम्
verses.iast:
parikrāntā mahī sarvā sattvavantaḥ ca sūditāḥ |
deva dānava rakṣāṃsi piśāca uraga pannagāḥ
na ca paśyāmahe aśvam te aśva hartāram eva ca |
kim kariṣyāma bhadram te buddhiḥ atra vicāryatām
verses.translation: " 'Entire earth is trekked and mighty beings like gods, demons, monsters, evil-spirits, fiends, serpents, naga-s are also eliminated, but we have not seen the ritual-horse or its stealer. What we have to do next. Let a thought be given in this matter. Let safeness betide you.' So said those princes to their father Sagara.

glosses.meaning: entire, earth is, over, run - trekked

glosses.itrans: deva daanava rakSaamsi pishaaca uraga pannagaaH
glosses.iast: deva dānava rakṣāmsi piśāca uraga pannagāḥ
glosses.devanagari: देव दानव रक्षाम्सि पिशाच उरग पन्नगाः
glosses.meaning: gods, demons, monsters, evil-spirits, fiends, serpents, naga-s
what is, to be done by us
in that matter, sagacity, be pondered on - give a thought to it.

verses.devanagari:
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा पुत्राणां राजसत्तमः |
समन्युरब्रवीद्वाक्यं सगरो रघुनंदन
verses.iast:
teṣām tat vacanam śrutvā putrāṇām rāja sattamaḥ |
samanyuḥ abravīt vākyam sagaro raghunandana
verses.translation: "On hearing that sentence of his sons, oh, Rama, descendent of Raghu, that exalted king Sagara infuriately spoke these words.

glosses.meaning: their, of his sons, that, sentence, on hearing

verses.devanagari:
भूयः खनत भद्रं वो विभेद्य वसुधातलम्
अश्वहर्तारमासाद्य कृतार्थाश्च निवर्तत
verses.iast:
bhūyaḥ khanata bhadram vo vibhedya vasudhā talam
aśva hartāram āsādya kṛtārthāḥ ca nivartata
verses.translation: " 'Let the earth be dug further, may safety be with you, and verily splitting open the surface of the earth you catch hold of the thief of the horse, and on achieving your purpose you may return to me.' In this way Sagara ordered his sons.

glosses.meaning: on achieving, purposes, return [to me,] also

verses.devanagari:
पितुर्वचनमासाद्य सगरस्य महात्मनः |
षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि रसातलमभिद्रवन्
verses.iast:
pitur vacanam āsādya sagarasya mahātmanaḥ |
ṣaṣṭiḥ putra sahasrāṇi rasātalam abhidravan
verses.translation: "On catching up the words of their father, the great-souled Sagara, his sixty thousand sons rushed towards the surface of the rasaa tala, the netherworld.
notes: The last but one mantle of the earth from its crust to its inner core, is called rasā tala, in the seven-tier planes called, atala, vitala, sutala, talātala, rasstala, pātāla.. These are not hells.

glosses.meaning: to netherworld's, surface, towards, rushed in.

verses.devanagari:
खन्यमाने ततस्तस्मिन् ददृशुः पर्वतोपमम् |
दिशागजं विरूपाक्षं धारयन्तं महीतलम्
verses.iast:
khanyamāne tataḥ tasmin dadṛśuḥ parvata upamam |
diśā gajam virūpākṣam dhārayantam mahītalam
verses.translation: "While digging the earth there they beheld a mountain similar easterly elephant named Viruupaaksha, which is bearing the eastern side of earth's surface on its head.

glosses.meaning: [eastern side of] earth's, surface, which is bearing

verses.devanagari:
सपर्वतवनां कृत्स्नां पृथिवीं रघुनंदन |
धारयामास शिरसा विरूपाक्षो महागजः
verses.iast:
sa parvata vanām kṛtsnām pṛthivīm raghunandana |
dhārayāmāsa śirasā virūpākṣo mahāgajaḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, Rama, the legatee of Raghu, that great easterly elephant Viruupaaksha is bearing the entire eastern earth along with its mountains and forests on its head.

glosses.meaning: with, mountains, forests, in its entirety, [eastern side of] earth

verses.devanagari:
यदा पर्वणि काकुत्स्थ विश्रमार्थं महागजः |
खेदाच्चालयते शीर्षं भूमिकंपस्तदा भवेत्
verses.iast:
yadā parvaṇi kākutstha viśramārtham mahāgajaḥ |
khedāt cālayate śīrṣam bhūmi kampaḥ tadā bhavet
verses.translation: "On certain occasions, oh, Rama of Kakutstha, when that great-elephant moves its head desiring respite in tiresomeness then earthquakes will occur on earth.

verses.devanagari:
ते तं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा दिशापालं महागजम् |
मानयन्तो हि ते राम जग्मुर्भित्त्वा रसातलम्
verses.iast:
te tam pradakṣiṇam kṛtvā diśā pālam mahāgajam |
mānayanto hi te rāma jagmur bhittvā rasātalam
verses.translation: "They circumambulated the great elephant in supplication, oh Rama, and on worshipping that elephant which is the protector of easterly direction they proceeded to netherworld duly splitting the earth.

glosses.meaning: easterly direction, protector of, to great, elephant

verses.devanagari:
ततः पूर्वां दिशं भित्त्वा दक्षिणां बिभिदुः पुनः |
दक्षिणस्यामपि दिशि ददृशुस्ते महागजम्
महापद्मं महात्मानं सुमहत्पर्वतोपमम् |
शिरसा धारयन्तं गां विस्मयं जग्मुरुत्तमम्
verses.iast:
tataḥ pūrvām diśam bhittvā dakṣiṇām bibhiduḥ punaḥ |
dakṣiṇasyām api diśi dadṛśuḥ te mahāgajam
mahā padmam mahātmānam sumahā parvatopamam |
śirasā dhārayantam gām vismayam jagmur uttamam
verses.translation: "After splitting the eastern direction then they split opened the southern direction, and even in southern direction they beheld an elephant that is similar to a very great mountain, and that is sustaining southerly side of earth on its head, and on seeing that mammoth elephant of venerable character, namely Mahapadma, they went into an inordinate astonishment.

glosses.meaning: they, in the southern, direction, even in
by head, [southerly side of ] earth, one which is sustaining

verses.devanagari:
ते तं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा सगरस्य महात्मनः |
षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि पश्चिमां बिभिदुर्दिशम्
verses.iast:
te tam pradakṣiṇam kṛtvā sagarasya mahātmanaḥ |
ṣaṣṭiḥ putra sahasrāṇi paścimām bibhidur diśam
verses.translation: "On circumabulating that elephant Mahaapada in supplication, they the sixty thousand sons of great-souled Sagara scooped out the westerly direction.

glosses.meaning: to it - to elephant, circumambulations, on making

verses.devanagari:
पश्चिमायामपि दिशि महांतमचलोपमम् |
दिशागजं सौमनसं ददृशुस्ते महाबलाः
verses.iast:
paścimāyām api diśi mahāntam acalopamam |
diśā gajam saumanasam dadṛśuḥ te mahā balāḥ
verses.translation: "Even in the westerly direction those great mighty sons of Sagara beheld an infinite and mountain similar elephant of western direction, called Sumanasa.

verses.devanagari:
ते तं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा पृष्ट्वा चापि निरामयम् |
खनंतः समुपक्रांता दिशं सोमवतीं तदा
verses.iast:
te tam pradakṣiṇam kṛtvā pṛṣṭvā ca api nirāmayam |
khanantaḥ samupakrāntā diśam somavatīm tadā
verses.translation: "Circumabulating that elephant namely Sumanasa in western side, and even on asking about its well-being, then they reached the northern direction duly digging the earth.

glosses.meaning: they, to it, circumambulations, on performing
its well-being, on asking, also, even
nectar, which has, that direction, or, which has more Soma juice because rituals are performed there

verses.devanagari:
उत्तरस्यां रघुश्रेष्ठ ददृशुर्हिमपाण्डुरम् |
भद्रं भद्रेण वपुषा धारयन्तं महीमिमाम्
verses.iast:
uttarasyām raghuśreṣṭha dadṛśur hima pāṇḍuram |
bhadram bhadreṇa vapuṣā dhārayantam mahīm imām
verses.translation: "In the northern direction, oh, Rama, they beheld Bhadra, a snow-white elephant with an auspicious body bearing northern side of this earth.

glosses.meaning: oh, Rahu dynasty's, best one - Rama

verses.devanagari:
समालभ्य ततः सर्वे कृत्वा चैनं प्रदक्षिणम् |
षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि बिभिदुर्वसुधातलम्
verses.iast:
samālabhya tataḥ sarve kṛtvā ca enam pradakṣiṇam |
ṣaṣṭiḥ putra sahasrāṇi bibhidur vasudhā talam
verses.translation: "On touching that elephant reverently and also circumambulating it, those sixty thousands sons of Sagara further burrowed to the surface of the earth.

verses.devanagari:
ततः प्रागुत्तरां गत्वा सागराः प्रथितां दिशम् |
रोषादभ्यखनन्सर्वे पृथिवीं सगरात्मजाः
verses.iast:
tataḥ prāk uttarām gatvā sāgarāḥ prathitām diśam |
roṣāt abhyakhanan sarve pṛthivīm sagara ātmajāḥ
verses.translation: "The sons of Sagara have then gone to the auspicious northeast direction, iishaana digbhaaga, Shiva sthaana, and all those sons of Sagara have tunnelled the earth rancorously.

glosses.meaning: auspicious, east, north, to direction, on going

verses.devanagari:
ते तु सर्वे महत्मानो भीमवेगा महबलाः |
ददृशुः कपिलं तत्र वासुदेवं सनातनम्
हयं च तस्य देवस्य चरन्तमविदूरतः |
प्रहर्षमतुलं प्राप्ताः सर्वे ते रघुनंदन
verses.iast:
te tu sarve mahatmāno bhimavega mahabalāḥ |
dadṛśuḥ kapilam tatra vāsudevam sanātanam
hayam ca tasya devasya carantam avidūrataḥ |
praharṣam atulam praptaḥ sarve te raghunandana
verses.translation: "But all those great-souled and great-mighty ones with terrible dash have seen the Infinite Vasudeva in the form of sage Kapila there in the northeast, and oh, descendant of Raghu, they have also seen the ritual-horse moving nearby that sage Kapila, thus all of the sons of Sagara obtained a matchless delight.

glosses.meaning: great-souled ones, of terrible dash, great mighty ones

verses.devanagari:
ते तं हयहरं ज्ञात्वा क्रोधपर्याकुलेक्षणाः |
खनित्रलांगलधरा नानावृक्षशिलाधराः
अभ्यधावन्त संक्रुद्धास्तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रुवन् |
verses.iast:
te tam haya haram GYātvā krodha paryākula īkṣaṇāḥ |
khanitra lāṅgalā dhara nānā vṛkśa śilā dharāḥ
abhyadhāvanta saṅkruddhāḥ tiṣṭha tiṣṭha iti ca abruvan |
verses.translation: "The eyes of the princes are agitated in fury in construing the sage Kapila as the stealer of ritual-horse, and they furiously dashed towards him wielding crowbars, ploughs, and various trees and boulders, and shouting at him, 'stay, stay.'

glosses.meaning: stay, stay, thus, they said - shouted, also.

verses.devanagari:
अस्माकं त्वं हि तुरगं यज्ञियं हृतवानसि
दुर्मेधस्त्वं हि संप्राप्तान् विद्धि नः सगरात्मजान् |
verses.iast:
asmākam tvam hi turagam yaGYiyam hṛtavān asi
durmedhaḥ tvam hi samprāptān viddhi naḥ sagarātmajān |
verses.translation: "You the malicious one, you have indeed stolen our ritual-horse, and in fact, you should know that we who arrived here are the sons of Sagara.' Thus Sagara's sons shouted at sage Kapila.

glosses.meaning: horse, you have stolen, you are, indeed
to here who have come, us

verses.devanagari:
श्रुत्वा तद्वचनं तेषां कपिलो रघुनंदन
रोषेण महताविष्टो हुं कारमकरोत्तदा |
verses.iast:
śrutvā tat vacanam teṣām kapilo raghunandana
roṣeṇa mahatā āviṣṭo hum kāram akarot tadā |
verses.translation: "On hearing their words, oh, Rama, the descendant of Raghu, then sage Kapila is beset with high wrath, and he boomed a 'hum' sound at them.

glosses.meaning: Kapila, their, that, sentence, on listening
hum [in dissent,] sound, he made - sage made the sound.

verses.devanagari:
ततस्तेनाप्रमेयेण कपिलेन महात्मना |
भस्मराशीकृताः सर्वे काकुत्स्थ सगरात्मजाः
verses.iast:
tataḥ tena aprameyeṇa kapilena mahātmanā |
bhasma rāśī kṛtāḥ sarve kākutstha sagarātmajāḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, Rama of Kakutstha, then that great-souled sage Kapila, rather Vishnu with unimaginable power, has rendered all of those sons of Sagara as heaps of ashes by virtue of his 'hum' sound." Thus Sage Vishvamitra is narrating the legend of Sagara to Rama and others. [1-40-30b, c]

glosses.meaning: of unimaginable power maha atmanaa = by that great-souled one
to ashes, heaps of, rendered as.
